sentences.text: Crm-9862-2017 on 26 October, 2017

Author: Debasish Kar Gupta
Bench: Debasish Kar Gupta

1
5 26.10.2017
C.R.M. No.9862 of 2017 p.d.
Re: An application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. affirmed on 20.9.2017 in connection with
Nabadwip Police Station Case No.308 dated 2.8.2017 under Sections 272/273/420/120B of the
Indian Penal Code.
In re:- Dipankar Saha .... Petitioner.

Mr. Himanghu De, Mr. Navanil De, Mr. Prasanta Kr. Bagchi, Mrs. Ayantika Ray ... For the
petitioner.
Mr. Pradipta Ganguly .... For the State.

At the very outset, the report prepared by the Superintendent of Police, District-Nadia is submitted before us by the learned Advocate for the State in terms of the order dated October 17, 2017 passed by the Vacation Bench of this Court.
Considering the aforesaid report, we accept the explanation given in the aforesaid report with regard to delay in forwarding the case diary to the learned State Advocate.
Heard the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the parties.
Perused the case diary.
The petitioner is in custody for about 85 days.
Investigation is still in progress.

It is submitted by Mr. Himanghu De, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner that the case has been initiated against the petitioner by the police authorities without jurisdiction in view of the provision contained in Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
It is further submitted by him that the petitioner has been harassing without any analytical report of the product, which he has been manufacturing and/or selling.

The above prayer of the petitioner is vividly opposed by Mr. Pradipta Ganguly, the learned Advocate CRM-9862-2017 on 26 October, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46393704/
1 for the State and he submits that the petitioner has a licence of manufacturing wholesale and retail sale of Chanachur.

The petitioner is found to have purchased some materials for preparation of Chanachur from Parley Biscuit Private Limited, which are not fit for human consumption and according to the prosecution case, those have been used for manufacturing Chanachur.

It is also submitted by him that the articles seized (pages 46 and 47 of the case diary) from the possession of the petitioner have already been sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory on August 2, 2017.

So far as the question of jurisdiction of the police authorities is concerned, we do not think that this is a proper Forum to agitate the grievance of the petitioner and to quash the proceeding and/or to pass any other consequential order.

So far as the other ground agitated by Mr. De is concerned, we are of the opinion that since the investigation is still in progress and the seized articles have already been sent to the concerned Forensic Science Laboratory, we are not inclined to allow the prayer for granting bail in favour of the petitioner.
Accordingly, such prayer is rejected and the application for bail stands dismissed.
(Debasish Kar Gupta, J.) (Arindam Sinha, J. )
